text: This is it — the final lesson of the entire course. Let's zoom all the way out and see exactly where T-SQL fits in the bigger picture you've been building toward this whole time.

Four stages. Source — where real transactions get recorded, every SELECT and JOIN from Chapters 1 through 9. Transform — where raw rows get reshaped for the warehouse, and Lesson 112 showed you T-SQL's own INSERT SELECT can literally BE that transform engine. Warehouse — querying the star schema you've spent this whole chapter learning. And BI tools — every chart Power BI or any reporting layer renders is ultimately backed by a T-SQL query underneath, whether it generated that query itself or you wrote it by hand.

One last query to prove the point. A join, a group by, a where clause that stays SARGable, a window function for a running total — running against a real star-schema fact table. That's five different chapters, working together, in one script.

And here's the thread that ran through every single one of those stages: performance tuning. The exact same execution-plan and statistics tools from Chapter 10 diagnose a slow query, no matter which stage of this pipeline it's hiding in.
From your very first SELECT statement in Lesson 1, to a production-shaped warehouse query right here — that's the whole course. Congratulations on finishing T-SQL Development. Well done.
